question: What portion of the original historical-native Brier change is due to the exact native context reset, versus the same next witnessed update without reset?
hypothesis: Posthoc engineering hypothesis: resetting the mixture and reshuffling the original context blocks produces an immediate old-readout discontinuity that is separable from the underlying witnessed native update; no scientific prospective claim is made.
scientific_evidence_class: UNPREREGISTERED_POSTHOC: Both original 99231 and 99247 development scores and context reset events were already observed. This is explicitly not new confirmatory or protected source.
predecessor_evidence: YGG-JEPA2-05 PR #1298 exact frozen consumed development; original DEV_NO_GO
Read-only source and block roster diagnostics PR #1298 comments 7023401268 and 7023581084
Native context mix reset source audit PR #1298 comment 7023728076

inputs.name: original actual JEPA2-05 continued state archival

frozen_design.split: original 32 old native episodes per seed, always the same fixed old-reference probes
frozen_design.ordering: exact 16 already observed archived new events per seed in original receipt order; no access to new source
frozen_design.data_budget: two already consumed archival states x 16 historical observed public consequences, zero new source actions
frozen_design.compute_budget: <= 15 minutes per OS including real cold source replay and full regression
frozen_design.capacity: same original native + four JEPA heads, two unused cloned future heads; no new learner
frozen_design.evaluator: NativeEpisodeExperience.context_forecast on original 32 old episodes, mean of transition and conditional terminal Brier per episode; 64 scored probability observations per seed

controls: original pinned cold restored model before any suffix
same post-update native state with old context as shadow, including old member weights and new event but excluding exactly the context reset
actual post-update native state including triggered context reset
metrics: published initial and final Brier reproduction to 1e-10 absolute
posthoc before/no-reset/after-reset Brier at every observed context-reset event
original native and 4 previous JEPA head full cold checkpoint source parity
same 32 old probes from unchanged prefix
per-platform CPU seconds and source/head/ledger hashes

classification_rules.supported: POSTHOC_DIAGNOSTIC_ONLY when exact published old Brier and original learned checkpoint restore, pre/post old-native source identity and same source event replay all pass; record signed actual-minus-shadow reset effect without calling it prospective science
classification_rules.mixed: POSTHOC_MIXED if source-compatible reproduction passes but one seed provides no identifiably isolated reset effect
classification_rules.negative: POSTHOC_DIAGNOSTIC_NEGATIVE if source-compatible reproduction passes and signed reset effects are <=0 for both seeds
classification_rules.invalid: REPRODUCTION_FAIL if any original/final published Brier differs by more than 1e-10, source/pin/provenance mismatch, original trained weights mutated, seed mismatch, unauthorized source call or replay control not exact
